content.body:
The Mk If version of the Blenheim was adapted as heavy fighter/attack aircraft from the light bomber it had started out as. It was equipped with a belly pack of four .303 caliber light machineguns in the bomb bay cavity, in addition to eight externally mounted 40 pound anti-personnel/light vehicle bombs.
Unfortunately, it proved to be very vulnerable against the 109s and 110s of the Luftwaffe when they finally met in combat, and was eventually withdrawn into alternative service as a night fighter where it would be unlikely to meet other fighter aircraft and perhaps fare better. Carrying their small bomb load in addition to the machine gun package, Blen Mk I's were able to play a role as light interdiction and support aircraft only during the early years of the war.
They were simply not versatile enough nor did they perform well enough to excel in any combat role in general. They do make useful bomber interceptors if the bombers are unescorted and the Blenheim's have gotten to altitude early enough to make the interception. The Bf 110 had a similar role for the Germans later in the war, when the Bf 110's were not competitive at any other form of combat. Of course, Bf 110s have a lot more firepower than Blen I's do.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Pilot 2 Top Gunner
